meaning: Squatina, see genus; squatina, Latin squatum, a name for angel sharks dating to Pliny the Elder, a Latin synonym of rhinus, an ancient name for sharks, from Greek rhinos “skin or hide of a beast” or rhínē “rasp”, both apparently alluding to a shark's rough skin
description: A flat, ray-like shark with broad wing-like pectoral fins, grey to brown above with small dark and pale markings, and eyes on top of its head. It lies half-buried in sand or mud and ambushes flatfish, skates, squid and crabs. Once widespread in the northeast Atlantic and Mediterranean, it is now Critically Endangered.
depth: Shallow coastal water to about 150 m
eats: Flatfish and other bottom fish, skates, squid and crabs
